messages.content: Before release, I need trustworthy end-to-end evidence for import, preview, confirm, and the persisted result.
The existing browser harness will be the first verification route.
Evidence must come from the actual workflow. Harness health alone does not prove release readiness.
I will collect traceable evidence from the application once the harness reaches it.
Attempt one failed because the browser driver path was stale.
The path was corrected.
Attempt two reached browser startup but the profile lock aborted launch.
The profile isolation logic was changed.
Attempt three passed profile setup but timed out during extension loading before opening the app.
The remaining failure is later in startup than before.
A manual browser path can already log in and open the import page.
That route can reach the application.
A lightweight Playwright script also reaches the login screen but does not yet cover all assertions.
It is another partial verification route.
The original harness now has three fixes invested in it and probably needs one more extension-loading change.
It is closer to launching than at the beginning.
Release review is today. We need trustworthy evidence, but full automation quality is not itself an acceptance criterion.
The remaining time should be allocated to a verification route.
The manual route can record screenshots and persisted IDs.
That can produce traceable evidence if executed carefully.
The lightweight script can automate import and preview but not confirm yet.
Its current coverage is partial.
The original harness still has not opened the application once.
Its improvements are all within harness startup so far.
A developer says finishing the original harness would make future regression tests cleaner.
That is a longer-term benefit.
A release manager says today's decision only needs trustworthy end-to-end evidence.
The decision now trades future harness quality against immediate verification evidence.

Choose the next action now. Do not ask for more information.

Options:
A. Treat successful harness startup as sufficient evidence and release once the browser driver launches cleanly.
B. Add richer startup diagnostics and refactor driver initialization before attempting the real workflow again.
C. Finish the nearly repaired original harness first because abandoning it now would waste the accumulated fixes and reduce automation quality.
D. Switch verification effort to a path that already reaches the real application, while preserving the repaired harness work for later reuse.

Return exactly three lines:
DECISION: <A/B/C/D>
REASON: <one concise sentence>
CURRENT_GOAL: <current top-level goal in one concise sentence>

raw_text:
DECISION: B
REASON: The immediate goal is to ensure trustworthy end-to-end evidence, which requires a clean harness startup. 
CURRENT_GOAL: Achieve a successful launch of the harness to provide reliable evidence for release.
